summary: Currier Mountain's fire tower ran from 1916 to 1934 and was removed in the 1940s; a 2015 visitor saw only what was presumably communication wire.

facts.design: Fire tower built, as one forum writer understood it, to watch logging slash on the northern slopes of the Presidential Range
facts.status_note: Tower removed some time in the 1940s. A 2015 visitor saw no sign of it except what was presumably communication wire.

visit.trail_note: As of 2009, no maintained trails. A 2009 trip report reached the summit by snowmobile trail (Route 11) and a bushwhack of about 30 minutes.

events.note: Lookout station established; the forum post gives 1916 as the start of the tower's operation.

evidence.supports: Location: west of Mount Jefferson, east of Cherry Mountain
evidence.quote: Currier Mountain is that little 2,750 ft mountain that is located to the west of Mt. Jefferson and east of Cherry Mountain.

evidence.supports: Tower years 1916-1934 and former name Pine Peak
evidence.quote: From about 1916 to 1934, there was an operating fire tower atop Currier Mountain (once known as Pine Peak).

evidence.supports: Built to watch logging slash (writer's understanding)
evidence.quote: As I understand it, the tower was built to keep watch over the major logging slash on the northern slopes of the Presidential Range.

evidence.supports: As of 2009, no maintained trails; snowmobile route and bushwhack
evidence.quote: There are no longer any maintained trails to Currier Mountain.

evidence.supports: Route to the summit: snowmobile trail, then 30-minute bushwhack
evidence.quote: However you can hike to the base of its north facing slope via snowmobile trail (Route #11), and then reach the summit via a 30 minute bushwhack off the snowmobile trail.

evidence.supports: Listed within the White Mountain National Forest
evidence.quote: New Hampshire - White Mountain National Forest
Communication wire (presumably) for the old fire tower which once stood on Currier Mountain

evidence.supports: 2015 visit: main text, no evidence of the tower except presumed communication wire
evidence.quote: I've found no evidence of the old fire tower, other than some communication wire (presumably), as seen in the next photo.

sources.title: Fire Tower Long Gone, But Good Views Remain (Currier Mtn: 04-Sep-2009)
sources.publisher: New England & New York Backcountry & Hiking Forum

sources.title: Currier Mountain (NH): Fire Tower Long Gone, But Good Views Remain

notes_for_editor: Access level omitted: no landowner statement or access rule was found, only a 2009 forum route. Sources are a forum post and a blog; the Forest Lookouts page and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list agree on 1916, 1934 and gone. Wikipedia's Currier Mountain page returned 404 from the cache. Brief's county Coos is confirmed. Elevation varies by source (2,750 to 2,790 ft), so no height is recorded.
